caption: A sheet of coloured paper is cut in half with scissors, and the two halves fall apart on the table.

sa.check: A sheet of coloured paper and a pair of scissors are present.
The scissors cut across the sheet.
The sheet ends up as two separate pieces.
The pieces lie apart on a table.
The cut runs through the sheet roughly in half rather than snipping a corner.
The cut comes first and the halves separate after it.

pc.expect: The paper parts exactly where the blades close and only as far as they have closed; the cut edge advances with the blades.
pc.fail: The blades close through the paper and it stays whole; or the sheet splits ahead of the blades or along a line the blades never touched; or the paper is already in two before the scissors reach it.

pc.expect: Once cut, the edges stay cut; the two pieces separate and do not rejoin.
pc.fail: A cut heals or the halves fuse back into one sheet; or the cut line shifts position after it is made.

pc.expect: Freed parts of the paper drop or slide down onto the table and stay there.
pc.fail: A half hangs in the air unsupported; or drifts upward; or slides across the table on its own after settling.

pc.expect: The paper behaves as a thin sheet: it flexes, its cut edge is a clean line, and the scissors stay rigid.
pc.fail: The paper stretches like rubber before parting; or shatters like glass; or the scissor blades bend or pass through each other.

pc.expect: One sheet becomes exactly two pieces that together make up the original; the scissors stay one pair.
pc.fail: A third piece appears or a half vanishes; or the pieces change size after the cut; or the scissors duplicate or merge with the paper; or the blades pass through the hand.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The paper's colour and the table stay the same on both pieces.
pc.fail: One half changes colour; or the paper's printed side changes; or the table surface shifts.
